Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/2$ | ${e}^{2}/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e/2}^{{e}^{2}/2}\frac{2}{3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{e/2}^{{e}^{2}/2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$
